newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar seen testing resistance at around 117 yen.
newsitem.headline: Dollar seen testing resistance at around 117 yen.

text.p: The dollar is likely to face a resistance at around 117 yen in Asia on Tuesday, while it may experience profit-taking against the mark before any further rally after Monday's steep gains, dealers said.
Japanese exporters and investors could move to sell dollars heavily near 117 yen, although the downside could be well-sustained due to strong bargain-hunting demand.

"It is likely to head toward 117 yen but the question is how much it can absorb selling orders around there," said a dealer at a Japanese bank. "Besides offers by exporters, there will be potentially strong selling demand there," he added.
He said 117 yen was a level at which Japanese exporters could exchange dollars for yen well above 115 yen through forward sales contracts.

The downside could be well-supported at around 116.30 yen, which was an intra-day low in New York on Monday. Expectations that Japan's interest rates are unlikely to be altered this month could support the dollar against the yen.

Movements in European currencies will continue to be the main theme in the currency market after Sunday's French election result raised concerns about enlarged EMU membership and a weak euro, sparking a spate of mark selling overnight.
"The basic trend is to sell European currencies and buy the U.S. dollar," said a trust bank dealer.

The dollar may ease slightly against the mark in Asia due to profit-taking after a recent quick rally, but there will be a further rally after operators lighten their positions, he said. Trading may be subdued amid a lack of fresh factors if speculators stay on the sidelines, he added.
"The dollar is likely to benefit as a safe haven currency amid uncertainty in Europe and the slim prospect of there being a rise in Japanese interest rates any time soon," the dealer said.
